description: Zero-knowledge proofs decomposed. Interactive vs non-interactive. zk-SNARKs (Groth16, PLONK), zk-STARKs. R1CS + arithmetisation. Trusted setup vs transparent. Applications: privacy (Zcash), scaling (zk-rollups), verifiable compute, identity.

sub_mechanisms.name: completeness_soundness_zero_knowledge
sub_mechanisms.definition: ZK proof properties: completeness (true statement provable), soundness (false statement not provable except negligible probability), zero-knowledge (proof reveals nothing beyond truth).
sub_mechanisms.why: Defining trio. All three required. Computational variants: relaxed soundness/ZK based on hardness assumptions. Strong versions for non-interactive.

sub_mechanisms.name: interactive_vs_non_interactive
sub_mechanisms.definition: Interactive: prover + verifier exchange messages. Non-interactive: single message (NIZK).
sub_mechanisms.why: Non-interactive practical. Fiat-Shamir transformation makes interactive into NIZK using hash function. Standard in blockchain (no interactive verifier).

sub_mechanisms.name: zk_SNARK_succinct
sub_mechanisms.definition: Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-interactive Argument of Knowledge. Proof size constant (~200 bytes) regardless of computation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Practical for blockchain. Verifier work O(1). Cost: trusted setup ceremony. Schemes: Groth16 (smallest), PLONK (universal setup), Marlin.

sub_mechanisms.name: trusted_setup
sub_mechanisms.definition: Some SNARKs need 'toxic waste' generated during setup, then destroyed. If retained, proofs forgeable.
sub_mechanisms.why: Required for Groth16. Mitigation: multi-party computation ceremony — only one honest participant required. Zcash 'Powers of Tau' ceremony.

sub_mechanisms.name: PLONK_universal_setup
sub_mechanisms.definition: Setup is statement-independent. Same setup serves any circuit up to size N.
sub_mechanisms.why: Setup amortised across applications. Foundation of many modern SNARK systems. Trade: slightly larger proofs than Groth16.

sub_mechanisms.name: zk_STARK_transparent
sub_mechanisms.definition: Scalable Transparent Argument of Knowledge. No trusted setup. Post-quantum (hash-based).
sub_mechanisms.why: StarkNet, Polygon Miden. Trade: larger proofs (10-100 KB vs SNARK's 200 bytes). Transparency + PQ resistance.

sub_mechanisms.name: R1CS_arithmetisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Rank-1 Constraint System. Express computation as constraints over field: a · b = c.
sub_mechanisms.why: Computation → constraints → polynomial → proof. Universal: any computation expressible as R1CS. Cost: blow-up factor depends on structure.

sub_mechanisms.name: circuit_compiler
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compile high-level language (Circom, Cairo, Noir, Halo2's DSL) to constraint system.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hand-writing constraints painful. Compilers expose constraint count + size. Active development; performance critical (proof generation slow).

sub_mechanisms.name: zk_rollup_scaling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Execute many transactions off-chain; submit single succinct proof to L1. L1 verifies; updates state.
sub_mechanisms.why: Scaling Ethereum. zkSync, StarkNet, Polygon zkEVM. Proof cost amortised across thousands of transactions. 100-1000x throughput.

sub_mechanisms.name: Zcash_private_transactions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Shielded transactions: amounts + sender + recipient encrypted. Validity proved via zk-SNARK.
sub_mechanisms.why: First major ZK deployment (2016). Demonstrates privacy + verifiability simultaneously. Note: most Zcash usage is transparent (UX cost of shielded).

sub_mechanisms.name: proof_generation_cost
sub_mechanisms.definition: Proof generation 100-10000x slower than direct computation. Memory + CPU intensive.
sub_mechanisms.why: The bottleneck. ZK rollup proofs take minutes-hours. Hardware acceleration (GPUs, ASICs) reducing. Active area of optimisation.

sub_mechanisms.name: ZK_for_identity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Prove age > 18 without revealing DOB. Prove member of set without revealing which member.
sub_mechanisms.why: Privacy-preserving identity. EU eIDAS framework + zkLogin patterns. Active deployment 2024+.

derivation_rules.name: ZK_separates_proof_from_data
if: a statement is proved via ZK
then: verifier learns nothing beyond truth of statement
derivation_rules.why: Defining property. Computationally enforced. Foundation of privacy applications (private transactions, anonymous voting, selective disclosure of credentials).

derivation_rules.name: SNARK_succinctness_enables_blockchain_scaling
if: proof is constant-size regardless of computation
then: expensive computation off-chain with succinct on-chain verification
derivation_rules.why: L1 verifies tiny proof in milliseconds. Off-chain computation arbitrary complexity. 1000x throughput via zk-rollups. The economic foundation of ZK in blockchain.

derivation_rules.name: trusted_setup_security_via_MPC_ceremony
if: trusted setup is performed via MPC with N participants
then: only one honest participant needed to ensure security
derivation_rules.why: Each participant contributes randomness; final result secure if any single contribution untainted. Zcash 'Powers of Tau' had hundreds of participants. Pragmatic mitigation of trusted setup concern.

derivation_rules.name: STARK_transparency_at_proof_size_cost
then: zk-STARKs are the alternative at larger proof size
derivation_rules.why: Trade: SNARK 200 bytes + trusted setup vs STARK 10-100 KB + no setup. PQ resistance also favours STARKs. StarkNet bet on this trade.

derivation_rules.name: proof_generation_is_the_bottleneck
then: proof generation cost dominates compute requirements
derivation_rules.why: Generation 100-10000x of native compute. Verification fast. Hardware acceleration (GPUs, future ASICs) addressing. Active research + engineering.
